question: Can original Harappa publications restore object-level contexts and physical observations for short inscriptions excluded from the principal prediction population?
outcome: The 81-target frame joins 72 objects. Original figures identify 24 targets, including all 22 copied tablets with excavation-unit/item keys and 66 displayed faces. Nineteen readable lower-face pairs occupy all eight declared arrangement classes. Two rectangular seals and four Beas vessel fragments provide comparison observations. All 97 integrity, accounting and frozen-replay checks pass.
challenge: Full CISI3.1 plates were unacquired; small renders obscured incisions; caption specimen order differs from catalogue order; concatenated derivative figure labels broke the first registration parser.
remedy: Followed original HARP author publications, joined complete registrations, preserved first-pass and native-raster reinspection separately, and retained missing/unreadable objects. The source-access and failure logs record the unsuccessful routes.
retry_when: Acquire identified adjoining-face photographs or 3D records, or previously unavailable source plates; freeze physical face order and incision coding before comparing published production groups.
